description: Per-line accepted residue for the diff-coverage gate (scripts/diff_coverage.py). Each entry names exact line numbers that are provably unreachable or not unit-testable, with the reason a test cannot execute them. The gate subtracts these from the failing set and prints every accepted line, so the residue stays explicit and reviewable. Entries whose lines become covered are reported as stale and should be pruned. Never use this to silence a line a test COULD cover - add the test instead. The list is expected to shrink toward zero or be deleted with the code it describes. Residue provenance: the SDK-convergence cli split (slices 1-6) moved and lightly edited ~6300 changed-statement lines; every line a test could reach was covered across the slices - what remains below is the audited tail.

internal/memory/markdown_source.go.reason: Four unreachable-or-untriggerable clusters. (1) 93-94: the write-directory's SECOND rejectSymlinkComponents(dir) call, immediately after MkdirAll succeeds on the SAME dir value the first call (a few lines above) already passed. MkdirAll only creates plain directories, never symlinks, and no code runs between the two calls that could swap a path component for a symlink - the second check is TOCTOU defense against a concurrent external actor racing a symlink into the path in that window, which cannot be deterministically synchronized from an in-process test. (2) 149-151: Scan's Parse(data) error branch (149-150) plus the closing brace the coverage gate counts as part of the same block (151). Parse (internal/memory/entry.go) has exactly two return statements, both `return e, nil`; its (Entry, error) signature carries an error return the current line-based implementation never produces. (3) 399-412: atomicWrite's tmp.Chmod/tmp.Write/tmp.Sync/tmp.Close error-branch bodies on an *os.File value local to the function, with no seam to intercept it. Triggering a live fd's Write/Sync/Close failure deterministically and portably (without an OS-specific unsafe technique such as an RLIMIT_FSIZE trip, which raises SIGXFSZ and kills the test process by default) is not achievable from this test package; TestAtomicWriteRejectsCanceledContext and TestAtomicWrite_RenameFailsWhenDestinationIsADirectory already cover the two atomicWrite error paths that ARE reachable (context cancellation before CreateTemp, and os.Rename's error after a real directory-collision precondition).

internal/ui/screen/conversation/thread.g.reason: threadDialogKey's post-hideComposer fallthrough (routeThreadDialogArrows then s.thread.Update). Dead given the current call graph: openThread's only two SetHideComposer calls (lines 219, 247) both pass true, and nothing ever flips s.thread.hideComposer back to false while s.thread is non-nil - dismissModals resets hideComposer only on the OUTER screen (session.go:115) after calling closeThread(), which nils s.thread rather than un-hiding its composer. So the guard three lines above (`if s.thread.hideComposer { return s, nil }`) is unconditionally true whenever this function is reached with a non-nil thread, and this block can never run. TestThreadDialogScrollKey_TabFocusesNextInHiddenComposerDialog and its shift+tab sibling pin the hidden-composer path this guard always takes instead.
